rights_duties.summary_en: Experts may request adequate materials, choose appropriate methods and reach independent conclusions. They must follow professional procedures, meet the request and deadline, preserve materials and maintain confidentiality. Statutory refusal and conflict grounds must be assessed.

procedures.scope: Shared judicial-expertise requirements under Law 105/2025/QH15. Route-specific procedural-code rules remain unverified. Examinations accepted and performed before 1 May 2026 remain subject to the transition in article 45(4).

statute.title_en: Law 105/2025/QH15 on Judicial Expertise, effective 1 May 2026; transitional cases remain subject to article 45

open_questions: Current Criminal Procedure Code provisions on appointment, questions, expert participation and supplementary/repeat examination remain to be verified, including amendments through 2026.
Current Civil Procedure Code article 102 and related appointment, question-setting and participation rules remain to be verified.
Article 35 signature, institutional endorsement and digital-signature formalities, and sector-specific forms under the 2026 implementing rules require further review.
Law 105/2025/QH15 replaced the 2012 expert law on 1 May 2026, subject to article 45. Determine the governing regime for examinations already accepted and performed before that date.
Criminal Code offence elements and penalties for false expert conclusions, and any prescribed warning or undertaking, remain unverified.
Electronic Transactions Law 2023, implementing decrees, trust-service and timestamp status, and the signature verification requirements remain unverified.
Vietnamese TCVN adoption of ISO/IEC 27037/27041/27042/27043 and Ministry of Public Security digital-forensic requirements remain unverified.
